subsections.title: Introduction
subsections.content: São Tomé and Príncipe (STP) is a small, stable island nation in the Gulf of Guinea off the west coast of Central Africa. With a population of approximately 232,000 and a projected GDP growth of 3.1% in 2025, STP is increasingly attracting foreign nationals through investor -friendly immigration policies, its natural beauty, and its strategic position within the Community of Portuguese Language Countries (CPLP). The legal framework governing immigration is anchored in Law No. 1/91 on the Legal Status of Foreigners, supplemented by subsequent government decrees. The Migration and Borders Service (Serviço de Migração e Fronteiras – SMF) is the primary authority over seeing entry, residence, and work permits. The eVisaST platform serves as the primary digital gateway for visa and permit applications.

subsections.title: Overview of Entry & Visa Categories
subsections.content: Before pursuing residency, foreign nationals must understand the entry pathway that applies to their nationality. STP recognizes the following categories:

subsections.title: Visa-Free Entry
subsections.content: Citizens of a range of countries — including EU member states, the USA, Canada, and recent signatories such as Ghana, Mozambique, Colombia, and Dominica — may enter STP without a prior visa for short stays. US citizens may stay up to 30 days; most other qu alifying nationals receive up to 15 days. These short -stay privileges do not confer any right of residency.

subsections.title: Electronic Visa (e-Visa via eVisaST)
subsections.content:
For nationalities not benefiting from visa -free entry, an electronic visa is available through the eVisaST platform. The e -Visa is a single -entry document valid for up to 30 days from the date of entry and must be used within 30 days of issue. It is valid for tourism, business visits, and transit. E -Visa holders do not qualify for residency; only long -stay visa holders may pursue residency status.

- Apply online at the SMF eVisaST portal.

- Upload a single PDF (under 2 MB) containing passport copy, travel ticket, and

accommodation or contact details.

- Save the generated process/reference number to track application status.

- No changes are permitted post -submission — accuracy is critical.

- Processing time: typically,  up to 7 days.

Visa Fees & Airport Stamping:  Upon arrival at São Tomé International Airport, you are required to pay a stamping fee in cash  to receive the official visa stamp in your passport. Please ensure you have the exact amount ready:

- €20 for a single -entry 1 -month Tourist Visa.

- €30 for a single -entry 1 -month Business Visa.

- Note: Children under 18 pay half the standard fee. ( Reference: São Tomé

Islands FAQ )

subsections.title: Business / Commercial Visa
subsections.content: Designed for commercial activities such as meetings, negotiations, or short -term engagements that do not constitute local employment. Valid for up to 30 days, available as single or multiple entry. Applications are submitted via the eVisaST platform using the same document upload procedure described above.

subsections.title: Long-Stay Visa (Visto de Longa Duração)
subsections.content:
Foreign nationals intending to reside in STP for more than 90 days must obtain a long -stay visa prior to arrival. This visa is the prerequisite for subsequent applications for temporary or permanent residence permits. Applications are submitted at STP emba ssies or consulates abroad, with a processing period of up to 30 days. The visa category determines the basis for the applicant’s stay:

- Subordinate employment (with a confirmed employment contract)

- Independent professional or self -employed activity

- Research or highly qualified professional positions

- Study, exchange, internship, or voluntary work

- Family reunification

- Investment or business establishment

subsections.title: Visa Extension Process
subsections.content:
If you need to extend your stay, the responsible authority is the Serviço de Migração e Fronteiras  (Immigration and Borders Service).

- Practical Steps for Extension:

1. Apply Early:  Submit your extension request 7 to 14 days before your current visa expires. Do not wait until the last day. 2. Visit the Immigration Office:  Go to the headquarters in the capital, São Tomé, and request an "Extension of stay" or "Visa extension." 3. Prepare Required Documents:  You will generally need:

- Your original passport.

- A copy of your entry stamp or current visa.

- A recent personal passport photo.

- Proof of accommodation (hotel booking or residential address).

- A tentative departure flight ticket or travel plan.

- Proof of sufficient funds (not always requested, but highly

recommended).

- A valid reason for the extension (e.g., tourism, personal

circumstances, or family visit). 4. Pay the Fees:  Extension fees vary based on the requested duration and are paid directly at the immigration office. 5. Wait for Approval:  Approval can be granted on the same day or take a few days, though it may take longer in certain cases.

- Extension Duration & Important Warnings:

- Duration:  Extensions are typically granted for an additional 15 to 30 days .

Longer extensions are possible but not guaranteed.

- Penalties:  Applying late may result in a fine. Overstaying your visa can lead to

complications upon departure or the outright rejection of your extension request.

- Note: An extension is an administrative approval granted by immigration, not

an automatic right. Pro Tip:  If you plan to stay for up to 3 months from the beginning, it is best to enter with your initial visa and a clear extension plan, or ensure you have strong documented reasons (like a business or family.

subsections.title: Health & Vaccination Requirements
subsections.content:
### 8.1.3.1 — Mandatory Vaccinations:

- Yellow Fever:  This is strictly required only if you are arriving from a country

with a risk of Yellow Fever transmission, or if you had a long transit in an at - risk African country. In this case, you must present an International Certificate of Vaccination (Yellow Card) . ### 8.1.3.2 — Highly Recommended Vaccinations:

- Hepatitis A:  Recommended to prevent infection through contaminated food

or water.

- Hepatitis B:  Recommended if you plan a longer stay or might be exposed to

medical procedures.

- Typhoid:  Highly recommended to prevent infection through contaminated

food or water.

- Tetanus, Diphtheria, and Pertussis (Tdap):  Ensure you have had a booster

shot within the last 10 years.

- Measles, Mumps, Rubella (MMR):  Important if you have not been previously

vaccinated. Malaria Prevention:  While there is no vaccine for Malaria, there is a low -to- moderate risk in the country depending on the specific region you visit.

- It is strongly advised to take prescribed anti -malarial medication before and

during your travel.

- Always use a strong, effective insect repellent.

(Reference:  CDC Guidelines for São Tomé and Príncipe

subsections.title: Flight Information (Egypt to São Tomé)
subsections.content:
- Departure:  Cairo International Airport (CAI)

- Destination:  São Tomé International Airport (TMS)

- Direct Flights:  There are no direct flights from Egypt to São Tomé. All routes

require 1 to 2 layovers.

- Ethiopian Airlines / ASKY Airlines:  This is one of the most common and

practical options for this route. Flights typically connect through Addis Ababa (ADD) and sometimes have an additional stop in a West African hub.

- TAP Air Portugal:  A popular and reliable route that usually requires a layover

in Lisbon (LIS), Portugal before heading south to São Tomé.

- EgyptAir & Royal Air Maroc:  You can also find combined itineraries using

these airlines, which usually connect through Casablanca (CMN), Morocco.

- One -Way Ticket:  Prices typically start around $750 to $900 USD  (approx.

36,000 to 43,000 EGP), depending on how early you book.

- Round -Trip Ticket:  Usually around $1,500 USD  (approx. 72,000 EGP).

- Travel Time:  Due to layovers, expect your total travel duration to range

anywhere from 16 to 22+ hours .

There are no direct flights that cover the entire route from Cairo to São Tomé via Angola, so your journey will be broken into two main segments. The Route, Airlines, & Travel Time:

- Leg 1: Cairo (CAI) to Luanda, Angola (LAD/NBJ):  * Airlines:  You will typically

fly with EgyptAir  (which occasionally offers direct flights) or Ethiopian Airlines  (which includes a layover in Addis Ababa). o Flight Duration:  If you manage to catch a direct flight, it takes about 6 hours . If you fly with a layover (like on Ethiopian Airlines), expect this leg to take anywhere from 10 to 15 hours .

- Leg 2: Luanda to São Tomé (TMS):  * Airlines:  Once in Luanda, you will

connect to a regional flight. The most reliable carrier for this segment is TAAG Angola Airlines  (the national airline of Angola), which flies this route a few days a week. o Flight Duration:  This is a relatively short, direct flight taking approximately 2 hours and 15 minutes to 2 hours and 40 minutes . Total Estimated Travel Time:

- Depending heavily on how long your layover is in Luanda, your total travel

time will generally range from 14 to 24+ hours .

- Note: TAAG Angola Airlines does not fly to São Tomé every single day, so you

may have a longer overnight layover in Luanda depending on the day of the week you arrive from Cairo. Approximate Prices:  Because this route combines major international flights with regional African carriers, the price can vary depending on whether you book the journey on a single ticket or piece it together separately.

- One -Way Total:  Expect to pay roughly $750 to $950 USD  (approx. 36,000 to

45,500 EGP).

- Round -Trip Total:  Generally,  ranges between $1,300 and $1,700 USD

(approx. 62,500 to 81,500 EGP). Pro Tip:  Pay close attention to your layover time in Luanda. If you have to self - transfer (meaning you booked the two legs on separate tickets and need to re -check your bags) or if you have a very long layover, you may be required to apply for an Angolan Transit Visa  in advance. Always ask the airline if your luggage can be checked all the way through to São Tomé! Pro Tip:  When booking flights with layovers in places like Lisbon or Casablanca, double -check if you will need a transit visa based on the layover duration and the terminal layout of those specific airports. subsections.title: Temporary Residence Permit
subsections.content: A temporary residence permit is required for any foreign national wishing to remain in STP for more than 90 days. It is typically issued for an initial period of one year and is renewable, subject to continued compliance with the conditions under which it was granted.

subsections.title: Eligibility
subsections.content:
To qualify for a temporary residence permit, the applicant must:

- Hold a valid long -stay visa appropriate to their purpose of stay.

- Demonstrate an ongoing legitimate reason to remain:  active employment

contract, registration of a business, enrolment in a recognized  study programme, or documented family ties to a lawful STP resident.

- Prove financial self -sufficiency or have regular income.

- Have no disqualifying criminal record.

subsections.title: Documentation Required
subsections.content: The following documents are generally required when applying to the SMF for a temporary residence permit: Document  Notes / Specifications Valid Passport  Minimum 6 months’ validity beyond the intended period of stay. All pages required. Long -Stay Visa  Confirming the authorized  purpose of entry (employment, study, investment, etc.). Application Form  Standard SMF form, completed in Portuguese or with a certified translation. Proof of Accommodation  Rental contract, hotel booking confirmation, or notarized  letter from host. Proof of Financial Means  Bank statements, employment contract specifying salary, or investment documentation. Criminal Background Check  Issued by the applicant’s country of origin; must be apostilled where applicable. Health Certificate  Certificate of good health; some circumstances may require a medical examination. Yellow Fever Certificate  Mandatory for entry into STP; must be presented at the border and at SMF. Passport -Sized Photographs  Typically, 2 –4 recent color photographs against a white background. Employment Contract (if applicable)  Must carry a favorable  opinion from the Ministry of Labor  confirming the absence of suitable local candidates. Business Registration (if applicable)  Company incorporation documents showing active investment activity in STP. Proof of Enrolment (if applicable)  For students: letter of acceptance from a recognized STP educational institution.

subsections.title: Employment-Based Temporary Residency: Additional Requirements
subsections.content:
For foreign nationals applying under the employment category, the Santomean government applies a local -labour preference policy. The employer must:

- Submit an employment contract to the Ministry of Labour.

- Obtain a favorable  opinion from the Ministry within 20 days, confirming that

the contractual terms meet legal standards and that no suitable local candidate is available.

- Comply with foreign worker quota requirements that priorities  local

employment.

subsections.title: Independent Professional / Investor Residency
subsections.content:
For self -employed professionals and investors, the applicant must demonstrate:

- Evidence of registered foreign investment or sufficient capital to sustain

independent activity.

- Professional qualifications where the activity requires them.

- A clear business or professional plan aligned with STP’s development

priorities (tourism, agriculture, renewable energy, and infrastructure).

subsections.title: Application Procedure
subsections.content: The application for a temporary residence permit is made in person at the SMF office in São Tomé, following legal entry into the country: 1. Step 1 — Obtain Long -Stay Visa: Apply at the nearest STP embassy or consulate in your home country before travelling. 2. Step 2 — Enter STP: Present your long -stay visa and yellow fever certificate at the port of entry. Ensure your passport has at least 6 months’ validity. 3. Step 3 — Compile Documentation: Gather all required documents, ensuring all foreign -language documents are translated into Portuguese by a certified translator. Have apostilles applied as required. 4. Step 4 — Submit to SMF: Present your application in person at the Serviço de Migração e Fronteiras (SMF) office. Pay the applicable processing fee. 5. Step 5 — Await Processing: Processing times can vary. Bureaucratic delays are common; applicants should submit early and allow a generous lead time. 6. Step 6 — Collect Permit: Upon approval, collect your temporary residence card from SMF. This document must be kept on your person at all times. 7. Step 7 — Renew Annually: The permit is typically valid for one year. Renewal applications should be initiated at least 30 days before expiry.

subsections.title: Permanent Residence Permit
subsections.content: Permanent residency in STP may be obtained after five years of continuous and lawful temporary residence. This represents the standard residency pathway for long -term foreign nationals, including workers, self -employed professionals, and family members.

subsections.title: Eligibility Criteria
subsections.content:
- Minimum 5 years of uninterrupted legal residence in STP under a valid

temporary residence permit.

- Demonstrated financial stability: steady income from employment, self -

employment, or investment.

- No major criminal convictions or breaches of STP immigration law during the

residence period.

- Established ties to the country: employment, family, business ownership, or

property ownership.

- Basic working knowledge of Portuguese is strongly advisable, as the

immigration process is conducted in Portuguese.

subsections.title: Documentation Required
subsections.content:
In addition to the standard documents listed for temporary residency, permanent residency applications require:

- Proof of continuous and legal residence for the full 5 -year period (residency

permit renewal stamps, tax filings, employment records, or utility bills).

- Current valid temporary residence permit.

- Updated criminal background check from both the applicant’s home country

and STP judicial authorities.

- Evidence of financial self -sufficiency (bank statements for the preceding 12

months).

- Updated health certificate and yellow fever card.

subsections.title: Rights and Benefits
subsections.content:
Permanent residents of STP enjoy the following:

- The right to reside in STP indefinitely without annual renewals.

- The right to work without a separate work permit.

- Access to most public services and administrative rights afforded to citizens,

except the right to vote.

- The ability to sponsor family members for family reunification visas.

- Eligibility, after meeting additional criteria, to apply for STP citizenship

(typically after a further period of residence).

subsections.title: Investment Visa and Investor Residency
subsections.content: STP actively encourages foreign direct investment, particularly in tourism, agriculture, and renewable energy. Foreign investors who demonstrate job creation or meaningful contribution to the national economy may be eligible for expedited special residency  permits. Permanent residency for investors is available to those making significant contributions, such as establishing a business or funding infrastructure projects.

subsections.title: Citizenship by Investment (CBI) Programme
subsections.content:
New Programme — Effective 1 August 2025 (Decreto -Lei n.º 07/2025) For foreign nationals who wish to skip the standard 5 -year residency pathway entirely, STP launched a Citizenship by Investment (CBI) programme in August 2025. This represents the fastest route to legal status in STP.

- Minimum investment: USD 90,000 (single applicant) — non-refundable

contribution to the National Transformation Fund

- Family of 2 –4 members: USD 95,000 (+ USD 5,000 per additional dependent)

- Processing time: approximately 6 –8 weeks from complete application

submission

- No residency requirement, no interview, no language test

- Dual citizenship permitted; no requirement to renounce original nationality

- Process can be completed entirely remotely through a licensed agent

- Dependants eligible: spouse, children under 30, parents and grandparents

aged 55+

- First passports issued January 2026 following 27 approvals

- Passport provides visa -free or visa -on-arrival access to approximately 60 –70+

countries

- CPLP membership facilitates preferential treatment within Portuguese -

speaking states

subsections.title: CPLP Mobility Agreement
subsections.content: STP is a member of the Community of Portuguese Language Countries (CPLP). This membership provides STP citizens and certain CPLP nationals with preferential mobility arrangements within member states — including access to simplified residence permit proces ses in Portugal. However, CPLP membership does not constitute automatic residency or immigration rights in other member states; national immigration laws continue to apply.

subsections.title: Language
subsections.content: Portuguese is the official language of STP. All immigration processes, forms, and official correspondence are conducted in Portuguese. Foreign -language documents must be translated by a certified translator before submission to the SMF. Proficiency in Port uguese, while not formally tested at the temporary residency stage, is practically essential for navigating daily life and bureaucratic processes.

subsections.title: Yellow Fever Vaccination
subsections.content: A valid yellow fever vaccination certificate is mandatory for all travelers  entering STP, regardless of nationality. This requirement applies at the border and must also be presented as part of residency documentation.

subsections.title: Healthcare and Infrastructure
subsections.content: Medical services in STP are limited. There are no adequate trauma or ambulance services on the islands. Even minor health issues may require medical evacuation at the individual’s expense. All foreign residents are strongly advised to maintain comprehensiv e international health insurance including medical evacuation coverage.

subsections.title: Financial Considerations
subsections.content: The official currency is the São Toméan Dobra (STN), pegged to the Euro. International credit cards (Visa) can be used at selected ATMs, stores, and hotels. USD and Euros are widely accepted for exchange at banks. For exit from STP, a report is required wh en leaving with €10,000 or more; financial statements must prove that no more is being exported than was  brought in.

subsections.title: Processing Times and Bureaucracy
subsections.content: Like many small island nations, STP can experience delays in administrative processing. Long -term residency and work permit applications are particularly susceptible. Applicants should plan well in advance, allow buffer time before any business commencemen t date, and consider retaining a local legal representative or immigration agent to navigate the process efficiently.

subsections.title: Useful Contacts and Resources
subsections.content:
- SMF (Serviço de Migração e Fronteiras): Immigration and Borders Service (in-country applications).
- eVisaST portal: Online e-visa application and tracking.
- National health guidance: follow CDC travel advice and carry yellow fever certificate when required.
- Airlines: Ethiopian Airlines, TAP Air Portugal, Royal Air Maroc, TAAG Angola; verify transit visa requirements for each layover.

subsections.title: Hotels — São Tomé Island
subsections.content: São Tomé's hotel sector is anchored by a handful of dependable properties, ranging from luxury beach resorts to well -run mid -range options. Omali São Tomé (4 -star) Located near the airport at Praia Lagarto, Omali is widely regarded as the most operationally reliable hotel on the island. It functions as a largely self -contained compound with direct beach access, a pool, restaurant, and spa. First choice for business travelers  and first -time visitors who priorities  infrastructure stability — seamless generator backup and international card acceptance. Guest rating: 9.4/10 (Expedia). A 15 –20-minute  walk from the city center , or a short taxi ride. Pestana São Tomé (5 -star) The group's flagship São Tomé property. Beachfront location with an infinity pool, kayaking, snorkeling , and proximity to the city center . Guest rating: 8.0/10 (Expedia). Free airport transfers included. Pestana Miramar São Tomé (4 -star) An older colonial -style property set in dense tropical gardens, adjacent to the main Pestana hotel. Atmospheric and well -priced, with a large garden pool and access to the main Pestana facilities. Named by CNN as one of the 20 best places to visit. Generat or shared with main Pestana; generally reliable. SH Boutique Hotel & Hotel Kenito SH Boutique Hotel (~$85/night) is a newer, well -reviewed mid -range option rated Excellent (8.7). Hotel Kenito offers budget -friendly rates with a nice pool; manual generator switchover (2 –5 min outage during power failures). Good value for non - luxury stays .

subsections.title: Hotels — Príncipe Island
subsections.content:
Príncipe is serviced by two flagship eco -luxury resorts set within the UNESCO -listed Príncipe Biosphere Reserve, both approximately 2 km from the island's airport:

- Sundy Praia (5 -star) — premium eco -resort, holistic spa, immersive nature

walks

- Bom Bom Island Resort (4 -star) — boutique eco -resort on a private peninsula

Important: Cash is the norm on Príncipe. Card terminals are largely unavailable. Bring sufficient Euro cash before travelling to the island.

subsections.title: Airbnb & Self -Catering
subsections.content: Airbnb availability on both islands is active and well -reviewed (overall rating: 4.6 –4.8 out of 5). Key categories include: Ecolodges & Beach Bungalows Monte Mar Ecolodge (near Tamarindos Beach) and Jalé Beach bungalows in the south — from ~$20 –$60/night. Breakfast and Wi -Fi often included. Rated 4.67/5 with 75+ reviews. Organic Plantation Farmhouses Stays on vanilla and spice plantations with sea views and private beach access (Porto Alegre / Caué district) — ~$50 –$120/night. Restaurant and traditional meals available on -site. Forest & Nature Cabins (Neves area) Chalets with private bathrooms, panoramic sea views, and veranda. Rated 4.83/5 with 48 reviews. 30+ endemic bird species in the vicinity — the best sunset on the island. City-Centre Guesthouses (São Tomé capital) From $30 –$80/night. Walkable access to the Mercado Municipal, waterfront, and restaurants. Long -Stay / Remote Work Rentals Fully furnished monthly options with dedicated workspaces and kitchens. Special monthly rates available with single payment and no additional paperwork. A tourist tax of €2.10 per person per night is standard and charged on -site at most properties.

sections.title: Reservation Policies
sections.content: Booking Platforms:   Hotels.com, Booking.com, Expedia, Airbnb,Flatio  and direct hotel websites all active for São Tomé and Príncipe properties. Cancellation Policy:   Most major hotels (Pestana, Omali) offer fully refundable rates on standard bookings. Policies vary by room type and booking date — always check conditions at time of reservation. Check -in / Check -out:   Standard check -out is 12:00 noon (e.g., Pestana Miramar). Late check -out is available on request and subject to availability. Payment: The country operates almost entirely on cash, and ATMs do not accept international Visa or Mastercard,  International credit cards accepted reliably at Omali and Pestana. Hit -or-miss at mid -range hotels due to mobile network instability. Rent and large deposits should be negotiated and paid via international bank transfer to European accounts before arriving . Always carry sufficient Euro or Dobra cash to settle your full bill in case terminals fail on check -out day. Airbnb:   Standard Airbnb booking and cancellation policies apply. Tourist tax (€2.10 pp/night) charged on arrival. Peak Season Booking:   June –September and December –March. Book well in advance during these windows as quality properties fill quickly. Local Long -Term Leases: Standard local rental contracts often require an upfront security deposit equivalent to 1 or 2 months of rent.

sections.title: Where on the Two Islands — Location of Accommodation

subsections.title: São Tomé Island
subsections.content: The island is approximately 50 km long by 30 km wide. Accommodation clusters in four main zones: Zone  Character  Key Properties São Tomé Capital (north)  Urban, walkable, waterfront promenade  Omali , Pestana São Tomé, Miramar, SH Boutique, Kenito Tamarindos / Neves (north -west)  Beaches, endemic birdlife, quiet nature  Monte Mar Ecolodge, nature cabins (4.83 ★) Santana / Cantagalo (east)  Surf beaches, cocoa farms, turtles  Ecolodges, guesthouses Caué / Porto Alegre (south)  Wild beaches, organic plantations, turtles  Jalé Beach bungalows, organic farmhouses

subsections.title: Príncipe Island
subsections.content: Accommodation is centered  near Santo António (the capital) and the island's northern beaches. Sundy Praia and Bom are the flagship properties. The island is small (~140 km²), remote, and highly protected. Serviced by domestic flights from São Tomé (approximately 30 minutes, operat ed by STP Airways). Car hires  essential once on the island.

subsections.title: Available Means of transportation
subsections.content:
- São Tomé e Príncipe Taxis and Car Rental

Car rentals are available in the country and there are a few international companies that have a presence but the more popular options are often through local companies, which are cheaper and offer equally reliable services. The network of roads in the cou ntry is extensive, adding up to about 230 miles. That said, most of the roads are in poor condition and several are unpaved. If travelers are intent on renting a vehicle, they should consider a four -wheel drive, which is far better equipped to deal with th e unpredictable nature of many routes in the country. There are a few private taxi services in the country, mainly operating the route between São Tomé International Airport and the city center. There are also shared taxis in most of the cities, which are identifiable by their bright yellow color and can simp ly be flagged down at the side of the road. Journeys within cities have fixed prices and travelers simply need to pass the money to the front of the taxi at some point during the journey. The prices of journeys outside of the city need to be negotiated beforehand.

- São Tomé e Príncipe Trains and Buses

São Tomé once had a thriving railway system  but this network has since been abandoned. Today, there are no rail services in the country and while sightseeing, travelers may even stumble upon the ruins of a few old railway stations and abandoned carriages. There are no private bus companies or coach services in the country. The only way to navigate between regions is to take a minibus taxi, which can be flagged down in cities or found waiting at communal taxi ranks. The fares for long distance trips should b e agreed upon prior to departure as there are no set routes. Travelers who wish to navigate their way between islands can do so either by ferry or local airline. tome -and-principe/transportation

subsections.content:

subsections.title: Air Travel :
subsections.content: This is the quickest and most direct way to get from São Tomé to Príncipe.  STP Airways  and Africa's Connection STP  are two local airlines that provide flights between the islands. The flights typically take around 30 to 40 minutes.  This route offers  18 fli ghts per week, making it the most frequent air connection in Sao Tome.

subsections.title: Sea Travel:
subsections.content: For those who prefer or require a less expensive option and aren't constrained by time, there are boat services available. The journeys by sea can take anywhere from 6 to 12 hours, depending on the service chosen, the size of the vessel, and weather condit ions. This option is more prone to delays and cancellations due to weather, and it's important to be aware that sea conditions can be rough

subsections.title: Cuisine Overview
subsections.content: São Tomé's food culture is a vibrant blend of African, Portuguese, and tropical traditions. Staples include fresh grilled fish (barracuda, snapper), calulu (a rich stew of fish, dried shrimp, and palm oil), funge (cassava or plantain paste), and locally - grown cocoa and coffee. The Mercado Municipal in the capital offers affordable street food and fresh produce. Claudio Corallo's chocolate plantation is a celebrated artisanal destination.

sections.title: Important Financial Notes
sections.content:
- São Tomé is more expensive than most visitors expect for West/Central

Africa. Import dependency drives up costs significantly.

- The local currency is the Dobra (STN), pegged to the Euro. Euros are widely

accepted and practically essential for cash transactions.

- There are no functional international ATMs outside the capital. Bring

sufficient Euro cash for the entire trip before arriving.

- Tipping: taxi drivers do not expect tips; hotel porters appreciate 1 –2 STN per

bag; tour guides: 5 –10% of tour cost for excellent service. thechocolateislands.com, farandwild.travel, BudgetYourTrip.com, CityCost.org, Climates to Travel, Weather Atlas.

subsections.title: Airbnb Availability and Accommodation Options
subsections.content:
- Availability: The short -term and mid -term rental market is relatively small

but active, with around 19 active Airbnb listings in the capital district of Água Grande as of early 2026.

- Options: Independent volunteers can find 1 to 3 -bedroom furnished

apartments in the city center. For long -term stays, local real estate agencies (like KÉBÔ Imobiliária) offer formal leases for apartments and houses.

- Platforms: Beyond Airbnb, platforms like Flatio cater specifically to long -term

stays, digital nomads, and expats without requiring a deposit. However, as of early 2026, Flatio currently has no active inventory for São Tomé. Traditional hotel booking engines (Agoda, Booking.com, Expedia, Kayak) also list guesthouses and eco -lodges suitable for monthly negotiation.

subsections.title: Prices Monthly Budget & Accommodation Rates
subsections.content:
Living independently in São Tomé requires a higher budget than many other African nations due to heavy reliance on imported goods, but long -term housing is much cheaper than daily tourist rates. A.  Long -Term Local Rentals (Per Month)

- Budget / NGO Worker: Basic apartments on the outskirts of São Tomé city or

simple guesthouses in Santo António (Príncipe) range from €450 to €800 per month. The absolute lowest recorded average for a basic 1 -bedroom city center apartment is $211 per month.

- Standard 3 -Bedroom (T3): A 3-bedroom local family home averages $569 to

$650 per month. Local real estate listings offer T3 apartments with a sea view starting around €450 per month, while a furnished T3 house ranges upwards of €750 per month.

- Expat Standard (Solo Professional): If you require international standards

(generator backup, reliable internet, proximity to the airport or NGOs), expect to pay between €850 and €1,500 per month. B.  Short / Mid -Term Platforms (Airbnb, Agoda, Kayak, Flatio)

- Flatio (Long -Term Specific): Flatio specialises in 1 -to-12-month rentals with

online contracts and no security deposits. However, there is currently zero active inventory on the platform for São Tomé, making Airbnb or local leases the only viable options.

- Airbnb Averages: The Average Daily Rate (ADR) for an Airbnb is $52 to $56

per night. Booking a full month via vacation rental platforms averages around $2,710 — which is why negotiating local leases is preferred for volunteers.

- Agoda / Booking / Expedia: The average price for a standard guesthouse is

$43 to $53 per night.

- Lowest Recorded Short -Term Rates: The absolute lowest daily rates are

found on Agoda/Booking — e.g., "Casa de Ferias" for roughly $22 per night, or "Albergaria Porcelana" at $39 per night. D. subsections.title: Feedback from Previous Travelers and Volunteers
subsections.content: The Positives: Volunteers report highly rewarding experiences, noting the extreme safety of the islands, the welcoming nature of host families, and the unique opportunity to work in a pristine, "lost world" jungle environment. The Pitfalls: Independent travellers repeatedly warn about the absolute necessity of bringing all funds in physical cash due to the lack of ATM connectivity. Volunteers have also reported instances of erratic and disorganised hosts when using unofficial platforms like " Workaway", highlighting the importance of verifying your NGO or accommodation thoroughly before committing to a 2 -month stay.
